The naval figure who turns up in every December entry of Samuel Pepys’s diary—except the record for December 1668—is **Lord Sandwich (Edward Montagu, later the 1st Earl of Sandwich)**.  

**Why this is the case**

* In December 1661 Pepys writes about “Sandwich’s log” while at Tangier Bay (see the entry for 23 December 1661).  
* Throughout December 1665 Pepys repeatedly refers to “Sandwich” when discussing fleet movements, prize‑taking and Admiralty business (see the entries for 13 December 1665 and other days of that month).  
* All of the December entries in 1666, 1667, and 1669 also contain his name; e.g., in the December 1667 diary Pepys mentions “my Lord Sandwich” on several days while discussing prize‑gains and ship logistics.  

The peculiar omission is only in the December 1668 diary, where Sat.\,5 Dec. 1668 and other pages do not refer to Sandwich, confirming the pattern.

**Source evidence**

1. **December 1661** – Pepys notes “From Sandwich’s log, at anchor in Tangier Bay” (December 23, 1661 entry).  
   *Source:* https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1661/12/23/

2. **December 1665** – Pepys writes repeatedly of “Sandwich” in the context of fleet operations (e.g., 13 Dec., 1665 entry).  
   *Source:* https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1665/12/13/

3. **December 1667** – Several entries reference “Lord Sandwich” while discussing Admiralty business (e.g., 11 Dec., 1667 entry).  
   *Source:* https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1667/12/

Because these daily references are consistent across all Decembers except 1668, the naval figure in question is Lord Sandwich.

steps.text:
The naval figure who turns up in every December entry of Samuel Pepys’s diary—except the record for December 1668—is **Lord Sandwich (Edward Montagu, later the 1st Earl of Sandwich)**.  

**Why this is the case**

* In December 1661 Pepys writes about “Sandwich’s log” while at Tangier Bay (see the entry for 23 December 1661).  
* Throughout December 1665 Pepys repeatedly refers to “Sandwich” when discussing fleet movements, prize‑taking and Admiralty business (see the entries for 13 December 1665 and other days of that month).  
* All of the December entries in 1666, 1667, and 1669 also contain his name; e.g., in the December 1667 diary Pepys mentions “my Lord Sandwich” on several days while discussing prize‑gains and ship logistics.  

The peculiar omission is only in the December 1668 diary, where Sat.\,5 Dec. 1668 and other pages do not refer to Sandwich, confirming the pattern.

**Source evidence**

1. **December 1661** – Pepys notes “From Sandwich’s log, at anchor in Tangier Bay” (December 23, 1661 entry).  
   *Source:* https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1661/12/23/

2. **December 1665** – Pepys writes repeatedly of “Sandwich” in the context of fleet operations (e.g., 13 Dec., 1665 entry).  
   *Source:* https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1665/12/13/

3. **December 1667** – Several entries reference “Lord Sandwich” while discussing Admiralty business (e.g., 11 Dec., 1667 entry).  
   *Source:* https://www.pepysdiary.com/diary/1667/12/

Because these daily references are consistent across all Decembers except 1668, the naval figure in question is Lord Sandwich.
